narration.full_text: The timing and amount of hormones released by various glands is controlled by a feedback mechanism which is inbuilt in our body. For example, if the sugar level in blood rises too high, it is detected by cells of the pancreas. These cells respond by producing and secreting more insulin into the blood. As the blood sugar falls to a certain level, the secretion of insulin is reduced automatically. Now, let's consider what happens at the synapse between two neurons. At the synapse, the electrical impulse generated at the dendrites of one neuron is passed on to the dendrite of another neuron. This transmission occurs in the form of chemicals, released by the axon ending of the first neuron. Finally, let's look at an experiment to demonstrate hydrotropism. Hydrotropism can be demonstrated with any germinating seedlings, which are allowed to grow on the ground. The soil around the roots is separated by a polythene partition. The left side is kept moist and the right side dry. The radicle at first grows in a downward direction. After some time, the roots bend towards the moist soil. This bending is due to the movement of the germinating roots towards water.
